Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 1:

Naming the surah

• It is called Saba' (Sheba), because it contains the story of the people of Saba', the blessings Allah bestowed upon them, and the state of disbelief to which their condition led, and their end because of it.

From the aims of the surah

• It speaks of the denial of the disbelievers concerning the Hereafter and their rejection of resurrection, and it affirms the resurrection by the command to the Prophet (ﷺ) to swear an oath concerning it, and by disputing with them about its establishment, drawing their attention to Allah's power to create what is greater than them, from what they see before them and behind them of the heavens and the earth.

• It explains that the preservation of blessings comes through thanking them, and that their removal comes through disbelieving in them, and this is shown through the story of Solomon (Sulayman) and the story of Saba'.

• It establishes the Oneness of Divinity (tawhid al-uluhiyyah) by setting forth proofs of Lordship (rububiyyah), and it nullifies the worship of other than Allah by demonstrating that they lack the capacity for what Lordship requires.

• It establishes Allah's knowledge, and it commands belief in the Last Day, mixed with encouragement and warning, and calls the disbelievers to faith in Allah, to sincerity in worship directed to Him alone, and to reflection upon the matter of this Messenger who was raised up among them, while they know his conduct, his truthfulness, and his trustworthiness.

[Tafsir]

Praise be to Allah for His attributes, all of which are attributes of perfection, and for His blessings, both apparent and hidden, religious and worldly, to whom belongs the dominion of what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and to whom belongs complete praise in the Hereafter. He is the All-Wise in His actions, the All-Aware of the affairs of His creation.

He knows whatever enters the earth, such as drops of water, and whatever comes out of it, such as plants, minerals and waters, and whatever descends from the sky, such as rain, angels and books, and whatever ascends to it, such as angels and the deeds of creatures. He is the Most Merciful to His servants, so He does not hasten to punish their sinners, and the Oft-Forgiving to the sins of those who turn back to Him in repentance and put their trust in Him.

The disbelievers who deny the Resurrection say: "The Hour will not come upon us." Say to them, O Messenger: "Yes, by my Lord, it will certainly come upon you. No one knows the time of its coming except Allah, the Knower of the unseen, from whom there is hidden not even the weight of a small ant in the heavens and the earth, nor anything smaller than that or greater, except that it is recorded in a clear Book, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), so that He may reward those who believed in Allah, followed His Messenger, and did righteous deeds. For those there is forgiveness for their sins and a generous provision, which is Paradise."

The disbelievers who deny the Resurrection say: "The Hour will not come upon us." Say to them, O Messenger: "Yes, by my Lord, it will certainly come upon you. No one knows the time of its coming except Allah, the Knower of the unseen, from whom there is hidden not even the weight of a small ant in the heavens and the earth, nor anything smaller than that or greater, except that it is recorded in a clear Book, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), so that He may reward those who believed in Allah, followed His Messenger, and did righteous deeds. For those there is forgiveness for their sins and a generous provision, which is Paradise."

Those who strove to hinder [people] from the path of Allah, to deny His messengers, and to nullify Our signs, competing against Allah and opposing His command: they will have the worst of torments and the most painful of them.

And those who have been given knowledge know that the Qur'an which has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth, and that it guides to the path of Allah, the Almighty, who cannot be overcome and cannot be resisted. Rather, He has subdued and overpowered everything, and He is the Praiseworthy in His sayings, His actions and His legislation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 7:

Those who disbelieved said to one another in mockery: "Shall we direct you to a man (they mean Muhammad ﷺ) who tells you that when you die and your bodies are scattered in every direction, you will indeed be brought back to life and raised from your graves?" They said this out of their excessive denial.

Is this man inventing a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him, so that he speaks of what he does not know? The matter is not as the disbelievers say. Rather, Muhammad is the most truthful of the truthful. As for those who do not believe in the Resurrection and do not act for it, they will be in everlasting punishment in the Hereafter, and in far-gone misguidance from what is right in this world.

Have these disbelievers, who do not believe in the Hereafter, not looked at the greatness of Allah's power in what is before them and behind them of the heaven and the earth, which dazzles the minds, and that they encompass them? If We will, We could cause the earth to swallow them up, as We did with Qarun (Korah), or We could cause pieces of punishment to fall upon them from the sky, as We did with the people of Shu'ayb (Shu'ayb's people). The sky has rained fire upon them and burned them. Indeed, in that which We have mentioned of Our power is a clear sign for every servant who turns back to his Lord in repentance, acknowledges His oneness, and sincerely devotes himself to worship.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "The Simplified Exegesis") on Surah 34, verse 10:

And We gave David prophethood, a Scripture, and knowledge. We said to the mountains and the birds: "Glorify Allah along with him." And We made iron pliable for him, so it became like dough, which he shapes however he wills.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 11:

"Make full-length coats of mail, wide ones, and calibrate the rivets in the rings of the coats of mail. Do not make the ring small, lest it become weak and the coats of mail not be able to provide defence, nor make it large, lest it be heavy on the one who wears it. And work, O Dawud, you and your family, in obedience to Allah. Indeed I am, of what you do, All-Seeing; nothing of it is hidden from Me."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 12:

We subjected the wind to Solomon: it traveled from the beginning of the day until its midpoint a distance of a month's journey, and from the midpoint of the day until night a distance of a month's journey at the usual pace. We caused molten copper to flow for him like water, and he used it as he willed. We also subjected to him some of the jinn, who worked before him by the permission of their Lord. And whoever among them deviates from Our command, which We had enjoined upon them, to obey Solomon, We will make him taste the punishment of the blazing Fire.

The Jinn worked for Solomon whatever he wished: sanctuaries for worship, statues made of copper and glass, large basins like cisterns in which water gathers, and cooking pots fixed in place, unmoved from their positions because of their enormity. And We said: "O family of David, work in gratitude to God for what He has given you, and that is by obeying Him and complying with His command. And few of My servants are those who thank God abundantly." And David and his family were among the few.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 14:

When We decreed death upon Solomon, nothing indicated to the jinn that he had died except a termite (ḥarḍah) eating his staff, on which he had been leaning. So Solomon fell to the ground. At that point the jinn realized that, had they known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment and the arduous labor for Solomon, supposing that he was still alive. In the verse there is a refutation of the belief held by some people that the jinn know the unseen; for if they knew the unseen, they would have known of Solomon's death, and would not have remained in the humiliating torment.

The tribe of Saba' in Yemen had, in their dwelling place, a sign of Our power: two gardens, one on the right and one on the left. (It was said to them:) "Eat from the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him for His blessings upon you. Your land is good in its soil and pleasant in its air, and your Lord is Forgiving to you."

Then they turned away from the command of Allah and from giving Him thanks, and they denied the messengers. So We sent against them the overwhelming, violent flood, which destroyed the dam and drowned their crops. We replaced their two fruitful gardens with two gardens bearing bitter, foul-tasting fruit, and with a tree resembling the tamarisk that bore no fruit, and a few lote trees (sidr) full of thorns. That change from good to evil was because of their disbelief and their failure to be thankful for the blessings of Allah. And We do not punish with this severe punishment except the ungrateful one who exceeds the limits in disbelief; he is repaid for his deed in kind, measure for measure.

Then they turned away from the command of Allah and from giving Him thanks, and they denied the messengers. So We sent against them the overwhelming, violent flood, which destroyed the dam and drowned their crops. We replaced their two fruitful gardens with two gardens bearing bitter, foul-tasting fruit, and with a tree resembling the tamarisk that bore no fruit, and a few lote trees (sidr) full of thorns. That change from good to evil was because of their disbelief and their failure to be thankful for the blessings of Allah. And We do not punish with this severe punishment except the ungrateful one who exceeds the limits in disbelief; he is repaid for his deed in kind, measure for measure.

And We placed between the people of Sheba (Saba')—who were in Yemen—and the towns which We had blessed—which were in al-Sham (Greater Syria)—towns linked one to another, visible one from another. We made travel between them measured, from one stopping-place to the next, with no hardship in it. And We said to them: "Travel through those towns by night or by day, whenever you wish, secure, fearing no enemy, nor hunger, nor thirst."

Because of their insolence, they grew weary of comfort, security and abundant living, and they said: "Our Lord, make the distances between our towns greater, so that our journeys between them become longer, and we find no inhabited towns along our way." But they wronged themselves through their disbelief, so We destroyed them, made them an example and a subject of tales for those who came after them, scattered them completely, and laid waste their lands. Indeed, in what befell "Sheba" there is a lesson for every person who is steadfast in patience (sabbar) in the face of hardships and trials, and grateful (shakur) for the blessings of God Most High.

Indeed, Iblis (Satan) had a conjecture about them that was not certain, supposing that he would lead the children of Adam astray and that they would obey him in disobeying Allah. So his conjecture about them proved true: they followed him and disobeyed their Lord, except for a group of believers in Allah, who remained steadfast in obedience to Allah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 21:

Iblis had no power to compel these disbelievers into disbelief. However, the wisdom of God required that he tempt the children of Adam, so that what He knew from eternity might become manifest, and so that We may distinguish the one who believes in the Resurrection, the reward and the punishment from the one who is in doubt about them. And your Lord is Guardian over all things: He preserves them and will recompense for them.

Say, O Messenger, to the polytheists: "Call upon those whom you claimed to be partners of God and worshipped besides Him, from among the idols, the angels, and the humans, and turn to them with your needs. Indeed, they will not answer you. They do not possess even the weight of a small ant in the heavens or on the earth, and they have no partnership in them. And God has no helper among these polytheists in the creation of anything. Rather, God—glory be to Him and exalted is He—is the One who alone brings things into existence, so He alone is to be worshipped, and no one besides Him deserves worship."

The intercession of the intercessor will not benefit with Allah, the Exalted, except for the one for whom He has given permission. And of His greatness and majesty, may He be glorified and exalted, is that when He speaks by revelation, the inhabitants of the heavens hear His speech, and their bodies tremble from awe, to the point that they fall into a state akin to swooning. Then, when the terror has departed from their hearts, some of them ask one another: "What has your Lord said?" The angels reply: "He has said the truth," and He is the Most High in His essence, His dominion, and the loftiness of His station, the Great over everything.

Say, [O Messenger], to the polytheists: "Who provides for you from the heavens by rain, and from the earth by plants, minerals, and other things?" They will certainly have to acknowledge that it is Allah. And if they do not acknowledge this, then say to them: "Allah is the Provider, and indeed one of the two parties, we or you, is surely upon guidance, firmly established in it, or in clear misguidance, immersed in it."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 25:

Say: "You will not be questioned about our sins, and we will not be questioned about your deeds, for we are innocent of you and of your disbelief."

Say, "Our Lord will gather us and you together on the Day of Resurrection; then He will judge between us with justice. He is the Opener (al-Fattah), the Judge among His creation, the All-Knowing of what ought to be decided by it and of the conditions of His creatures; nothing about them is hidden from Him."

Say, "Show me, with proof and evidence, those whom you have joined with Allah and made partners with Him in worship. Have they created anything?" The matter is not as they describe. Rather, He is the One truly worthy of worship, having no partner, the Almighty in His retribution against those who associate others with Him, the All-Wise in His sayings, His actions, and His management of the affairs of His creation.

And We have not sent you, O Messenger, except as a bringer of good tidings of Allah's reward and a warner of His punishment, to all of mankind. But most people do not know the truth, so they turn away from it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 29:

These polytheists say, mocking: "When will this promise that you make to us come to pass, in which Allah will gather us and then judge between us, if you are truthful about what you promise us?"

Say, [O Messenger]: "For you is an appointed time, which will certainly come to you, and it is the appointed time of the Day of Resurrection. You will not delay from it for an hour to repent, nor will you advance an hour before it for punishment. So beware of that Day, and prepare for it its provision."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 31:

The disbelievers said: "We will never believe in this Qur'an, nor in what came before it of the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms." They have denied all the Books of God. If you could see, O Messenger, when the wrongdoers are held back before their Lord for reckoning, bandying words among themselves, each one casting blame upon the other, you would see a dreadful sight. The weak will say to those who were arrogant, who were the leaders and chiefs who went astray and led others astray: "Had it not been for you, we would have been believers in God and His Messenger."

The leaders said to those who had been oppressed: "Did we prevent you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals, for you entered into disbelief of your own will, choosing it freely."

The weak among them will say to those who were arrogant: "Rather, your plotting of evil against us, by night and by day, is what brought us to ruin. You used to command us to disbelieve in God and to set up rivals to Him in worship." And both parties will conceal their regret when they see the punishment prepared for them. We will place shackles around the necks of those who disbelieved. They are punished with this punishment only because of their disbelief in God and their evil deeds in this world. In the verse there is a severe warning against following the callers to misguidance and the leaders of tyranny.

And We never sent a warner to any town but its wealthy people, immersed in pleasures and desires, said: "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."

The above was a translation of the verse rather than the commentary. The commentary text reads:

And We never sent a messenger to any town calling people to the Oneness of Allah and to singling Him out for worship, but those immersed in worldly pleasures and desires among its people said: "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, O messengers."

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsīr al-Muyassar, "the Simplified Exegesis") on Surah 34, verse 35:**

﴿And they said, "We have more wealth and children than you, and Allah has given us these blessings only because of His pleasure with us, and we will not be punished in this world or in the Hereafter."﴾

Say, [O Messenger], to them: Indeed my Lord expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants and restricts it for whomever He wills, not out of love or hatred, but He does so as a test. But most people do not know that this is a test for His servants, because they do not reflect.

Your wealth and your children are not what will bring you near to Us in nearness or raise your ranks. But whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, those will have the multiplied reward for their good deeds. A good deed is rewarded tenfold, and up to whatever additional increase Allah wills. They will dwell in the high levels of Paradise, safe from punishment, death, and sorrows.

And those who strive to nullify Our proofs, and who turn people away from the path of Allah, opposing and contending [against Us], they will be in the punishment of Hell on the Day of Resurrection. The angels of punishment (al-Zabaniyah) will seize them, and they will not come out of it.

Say, O Messenger, to those who are deluded by their wealth and children: indeed my Lord expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants, and restricts it for whomever He wills, for a wisdom that He knows. And whatever you spend of anything in obedience to what He has commanded you, He will replace it for you in this world with a substitute, and in the Hereafter with reward. He, glory be to Him, is the best of providers. So seek provision from Him alone, and strive in the means that He has commanded you to take.

Remember, O Messenger, the Day when Allah gathers the polytheists and those they worshipped besides Him from among the angels. Then He will say to the angels, in rebuke to those who worshipped them: "Did these people used to worship you instead of Us?"

The Angels will say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, [far above] that You should have any partner in worship. You are our Protector, whom we obey and worship alone. Rather, these people used to worship the devils, most of them believing in them and obeying them."

Then on the Day of Gathering, the worshipped ones will possess no benefit or harm for their worshippers. And We will say to those who wronged themselves through polytheism and sins: "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."

When the clear verses of Allah are recited to the disbelievers of Makkah, they say: "This Muhammad is only a man who wants to turn you away from worshipping the deities that your fathers used to worship." And they say: "This Qur'an that you recite to us, O Muhammad, is nothing but a fabricated lie that you have brought from yourself, and it is not from Allah." The disbelievers also said about the Qur'an when it came to them: "This is nothing but clear magic."

We did not send down to the disbelievers any scriptures that they could read before the Qur'an, which would guide them to their claim that what Muhammad brought them is sorcery. Nor did We send to them, before you, O Messenger, any messenger to warn them of Our punishment.

And those before them denied, such as 'Ad and Thamud, Our messengers. The people of Makkah had not attained even a tenth of what We gave the earlier nations of strength, abundance of wealth, long life, and other blessings. So those earlier nations denied My messengers in what they brought them, and We destroyed them. So look, O Messenger, at how My rejection of them and My punishment of them turned out.

Say, [O Messenger], to these deniers and obstinate opponents: "I only advise you of one thing: that you stand up for the sake of Allah, in pairs and individually, and then reflect on the condition of your companion, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and on what is attributed to him. There is no madness in him; he is only a warner to you, a warner of the punishment of Hellfire before you endure its heat."

Say, [O Messenger], to the disbelievers: "Whatever reward I have asked of you for the good I have brought you, it is yours. My reward is only with Allah, who is Witness over all my deeds and yours; nothing is hidden from Him, and He will recompense everyone, each according to what he deserves."

Say, O Messenger, to the one who denies monotheism and the message of Islam: Indeed, my Lord hurls falsehood with the truth as proof, so it exposes it and destroys it. And Allah is the All-Knower of the unseen; nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in the heavens.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 49:

Say, O Messenger: The truth has come, and the great Law has come from Allah, and falsehood has departed and its authority has collapsed, so that falsehood has nothing left that could begin anything or bring it back.

Say, "If I go astray, the sin of my error falls only on myself; but if I stay on the truth, it is by the revelation of God that He reveals to me. Indeed, my Lord hears what I say to you, and He is near to whoever calls upon Him and asks Him."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 51:

If only you could see, O Messenger, when the disbelievers are terrified upon witnessing the punishment of Allah, you would behold a dreadful matter. There will be no escape for them and no way to flee, and they will be seized and taken to the Fire from a nearby place within easy reach.

The disbelievers said, when they saw the punishment in the Hereafter: "We believe in Allah, His books and His messengers." But how could they reach faith in the Hereafter, and how could they attain it from a far-off place? Between them and it there is a barrier. Its place is this world, and they disbelieved in it while they were in it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 53:

They had disbelieved in the truth in the world, and had denied the messengers. They hurl conjecture from a distant place, far from hitting the truth, having no basis for their false assumptions. So there is no way for them to hit the truth, just as there is no way for the archer to hit the target from a distant place.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 34, verse 54:

And between the disbelievers and what they desire, of repentance and returning to the worldly life so that they might believe, there is a barrier, just as Allah has done with their counterparts among the disbelieving nations before them. Indeed, they used to be, in the worldly life, in doubt concerning the matter of the Messengers, the Resurrection and the Reckoning, a doubt that produces disquiet and anxiety, and therefore they did not believe.
